traced.aspect: Why the referee AssignServer (189) never appears on the wire — trace of the LobbyManager state-pump (FUN_00468f60 @SADK 80321) and the 189 send/reply ticket routing
traced.summary:
The repo's prior referee model assumed the client sends a SECOND, distinct AssignServer(189) for the referee at match-start. That is REFUTED. The binary sends the type-4 AssignServer exactly ONCE, via the LobbyManager state-pump's one-shot, and that single 189 (server_type=4) IS the one observed on the wire during the login/list burst. There is no separate referee 189 to wait for.

Full chain (all [PROVEN] from build-34688 decomp unless tagged):
1. sizeof(LobbyManager)=0x5a8 (alloc FUN_006f2524(0x5a8) @SADK 79701). The pump's one-shot latch this[1].field_0x4 = LM+0x5ac and timer this[1].field_0x8 = LM+0x5b0 are zeroed in the ctor (SADK 79644-79645) and written ONLY by the pump (SADK 80319-80330) — nothing external ever sets them.
2. Enum (decomp comments 'Init..ConnectionLost' / '1=Disconnected..0xc'): Authorized=3, VersionChecked=5, LoadingGlobalData=6. So the pump's `if (5 < state)` = state>=6.
3. state>=6 IS reached in the revival flow — proven empirically: chat/UC works, which requires state 6→7 (LoadingGlobalData→GlobalDataLoaded). On the first state>=6 frame the latch is 0, so the one-shot fires: latch:=1, FUN_00468f60(ServerList, FUN_004625d0), timer:=0. The latch then stays 1 forever (timer never goes negative), so FUN_00468f60 is called EXACTLY ONCE.
4. ServerList is embedded at LM+0x54 (cast `(LobbyServerList*)&this->field_0x54` @SADK 79882) — so FUN_00468f60's param_1 is LM+0x54 (the decomp rendering it as `this` is an artifact; both FUN_00468f60 and the state-6 setup FUN_00468e80 index +0x6c as pGameServerManager identically). pGameServerManager = ServerList+0x6c = LM+0xC0 (FinalizeParser comment 'gameserver-manager at this+0x6c'). Pending guards +0xa4/+0xa8 = LM+0xF8/+0xFC are zeroed in the ServerList ctor (SADK 84299-84300) and written ONLY by FUN_00468f60 on success.
5. Inside FUN_00468f60 (SADK 83311): the +0xa4/+0xa8 guard passes (both 0 on the only call); param_2=callback ≠0 passes; it REACHES the send `(*(ServerList+0x6c)->vtbl[0x2c])(4,4)` = tincat3 FUN_10021830.
6. FUN_10021830 (@tincat3 23937) is the ONLY type-4 189 builder (the other 0xbd builder, FUN_10027630 @27658, is hardcoded server_type=2/cat 0x109). It builds 189 server_type=4, allocates an outstanding ticket of category 0x108 (FUN_1002a1c0 @30038 stores {category,userdata} keyed by ticket_id), embeds that ticket_id, and SENDS on the lobby CommLayer.
7. The referee callback fires ONLY for an inbound 170 whose MATCHED outstanding ticket has category 0x108: dispatch case 0xaa (170) @tincat3 26778 routes by ticket category iVar7; `if (iVar7==0x108) FUN_10021520(...)` @26846. FUN_10021520 @23744 then requires server_type==4 && server_subtype==5 → fires the callback with server_id → FUN_004625d0 @SADK 78286 writes LM+0x580. A 170 arriving via the server-list broadcast (no matching 0x108 ticket; iVar5==0 / cat 0xab) goes to the LIST parser (FUN_10020790), NEVER FUN_10021520 — regardless of its subtype.

The stub (sadk_lobby/dispatch.py 307-331) replies 192 (UsercommServerData) to the FIRST/only type-4 189 and sets conn._uc_assigned; it only emits the referee 170 on a SECOND type-4 189 (line 319 gate `_uc_assigned` already True). That second 189 never exists.
traced.reconcilesWithEmpirical: The client sends EXACTLY ONE type-4 189 because the only type-4 189 builder (tincat3 FUN_10021830) has a single live caller — the LobbyManager state-pump one-shot (FUN_00468f60 @SADK 83327), fired once and latched (LM+0x5ac, set 0→1 once, never reset). That single 189 (server_type=4, subtype=4, ticket category 0x108) IS the observed one in the login/list burst (188 201 204 161 171x2 105 55 *189* 56 157 — the 171x2/55 already run at state>=6, exactly where the one-shot fires). It is NOT a UC-only request and there is no separate referee request: the same 189 is BOTH. The stub answered it with 192 instead of a 170(type4/sub5) echoing the cat-0x108 ticket_id, so FUN_10021520 never ran, LM+0x580 stayed 0, FUN_00462910 + RefereeServerConnection::Login no-op'd, and the match froze at 'connecting to game server' after retries. No second 189 ever appears — at lobby entry or match start — because the one-shot latch guarantees the type-4 AssignServer is emitted exactly once for the whole session; the referee advertised as a 170 type=4/sub=5 id=60 on the server LIST is delivered with no matching 0x108 ticket, so it lands in the list parser, never the referee gate.

traced.answer:
The referee AssignServer(189) is NOT actually missing as a distinct message — the prior model's premise (a second, separate referee 189 at match-start) is wrong. The binary emits the type-4 AssignServer EXACTLY ONCE, and that single 189 IS the one you see on the wire during login/list setup.

Mechanism, end to end (all binary-grounded):
- The LobbyManager state-pump (SADK 80318-80336) runs a one-shot when state>=6 (`5 < state`; LoadingGlobalData=6). state>=6 is genuinely reached (chat works ⇒ state passed 6→7). On the first such frame the latch this[1].field_0x4 (=LM+0x5ac, ctor-zeroed @79644) flips 0→1 and stays 1 forever (the timer LM+0x5b0 never goes negative), so it calls FUN_00468f60 exactly once. Answer to (a): YES, reached, latch unset on entry, fired once.
- FUN_00468f60 (param_1 = the embedded ServerList at LM+0x54) passes its guard: ServerList+0xa4/+0xa8 (=LM+0xF8/+0xFC) are 0 (ctor-zeroed @84299-84300; written only by this fn on success). So it does NOT bail — answer to (b): the guard does not block. It reaches the send `(*(ServerList+0x6c)->vtbl[0x2c])(4,4)` = tincat3 FUN_10021830, the ONLY type-4 189 builder, which allocates an outstanding ticket of category 0x108 and transmits on the (by-now-established) lobby CommLayer. Answer to (c): the send connection is valid at state>=6 (the same lobby conn that completed login), so the 189 DOES leave — and indeed it is the 189 observed in the capture.

The single most likely reason the referee never engages: the client's referee callback (FUN_10021520 → writes LM+0x580 via FUN_004625d0) is reachable ONLY when an inbound 170 is delivered as the matched reply to that cat-0x108 AssignServer ticket AND carries server_type==4 && server_subtype==5 (tincat3 26846 routes by ticket category 0x108; 23751 checks 4/5). The stub instead answered the (only) 189 with UsercommServerData(192), and its referee-170 branch is gated to fire only on a SECOND type-4 189 (dispatch.py 319, requires _uc_assigned already True). Because the pump's one-shot latch makes the type-4 AssignServer a once-per-session event, that second 189 can never arrive. Net: 189 sent → 192 reply (wrong) → FUN_10021520 never runs → LM+0x580 stays 0 → RefereeServerConnection::Login no-ops → freeze.

The fix is server-side and needs no second 189: reply to the FIRST/only type-4 AssignServer(189) on the lobby connection with a GameServerData(170) that echoes the SAME ticket_id and carries server_type=4, server_subtype=5, and the referee's id/ip:port — instead of (or selected over) the 192. The referee advertised on the server LIST (type4/sub5, id 60) is useless for this because list-broadcast 170s carry no matching 0x108 ticket and are routed to the list parser, never the referee gate. (Note this changes stub wire behavior ⇒ HARNESS mutation gate / Engagement Record applies; one live read-only capture should confirm the reply 170 with the matching ticket_id flips LM+0x580.)

traced.aspect: Where does LobbyManager+0x580 (the referee server address) REALLY come from? Trace FUN_004625d0's param_2 to its producer (server_id via AssignServer→170, or the [Lobby] url 8777, or other); read tincat3 FUN_10021520; rule the 8777 url IN/OUT for the TinCat RefereeServerConnection; conclude exactly what the stub must deliver so *(LM+0x580)!=0 and FUN_00462910 connects to OUR referee.
traced.summary: DEFINITIVE: *(LM+0x580) is a server_id delivered by the AssignServer(189)→GameServerData(170, ticket-category 0x108) callback path — option (a). It is NOT derived from the [Lobby] url 8777 (option b), and NOT from anything else (c is ruled out). FULL CHAIN, all in build 34688 (the running game): (1) LobbyManager_StatePump_Tick, once state>5 (>=LoadingGlobalData) and the one-shot latch this[1].field_0x4==0, calls FUN_00468f60(ServerList=LM+0x54, callback=FUN_004625d0). (2) FUN_00468f60 bails if (LM+0x54)+0xa4/+0xa8 already set; else calls pGameServerManager(ServerList+0x6c)->vtbl[0x2c](4,4) = tincat3 FUN_10021830, which builds NETMSG 0xBD(189) with server_type=4 (param_1) [wire server_subtype comes from a stale register; ticket-data byte=param_2=4], registers a fresh ticket under category 0x108 (FUN_1002a1c0 + AssignServerTicketData), and SENDS it. If that send returns success, FUN_00468f60 stores the callback as pending at (LM+0x54)+0xa4. (3) The REPLY must be NETMSG 0xAA(170) carrying the SAME ticket_id. tincat3 receive (switch on msg-type @ ~25847; case 0xaa @ 26778) resolves ticket_id→category via FUN_1002a240; when category==0x108 it calls FUN_10021520(GetType, &descriptor). (4) FUN_10021520 @23744 gates EXACTLY on descriptor.server_type==4 (param_1[10], desc+0x28) AND descriptor.server_subtype==5 ((int)param_1+0x29); on match it fires the assigned-server observer callback (*(*piVar1+0x20))(&local_8, *param_1, 0), passing descriptor[0] = the server_id. (5) That observer reaches SADK FUN_004625d0, which writes that server_id to LM+0x580 (and sets the 60000ms keep-alive at +0x588). (6) FUN_00462910 (gated *(LM+0x580)!=0) resolves the server_id to an address via pComm(LM+0x50)->vtbl[0x38](id) (Resolve) + vtbl[0x18](id) (get handle) and binds it into RefereeServerConnection(LM+0x490)+0x34; then RefereeServerConnection::Login dials it. THE 8777 [Lobby] url is a DIFFERENT subsystem: FUN_0040a390 + the network.ini loader @~28480 build ONE NComm Net-Driver/Reconnector settings object (also holds [Reconnector]timesClientRetries=5, the referee's 5-retry budget, and [Lobby]patchlevel). The url feeds the NComm net-driver's master/'site' bootstrap logon — 'SendLogonRequest: Connecting to site' lives in tincat3 FUN_10004660, the GENERIC TinCat ConnectionManager connect (0xDABAFBEF LOGMEON) used for the initial site connection — NOT the referee. The referee endpoint is resolved purely from the server_id cached in pComm's table (the type-4 RegObserverServerList).
traced.reconcilesWithEmpirical: The single type-4/sub-4 AssignServer(189) the client emits during login IS the referee assignment — it is the ONLY GameServerManager->vtbl[0x2c] call in all of SADK.exe with (server_type,server_subtype)=(4,4) (line 83327, inside FUN_00468f60), and tincat3 only ever builds a type-4 189 via FUN_10021830 (the other 189-builder, FUN_10027630, hardcodes server_type=2/category 0x109). So that ONE 189 expects a 170(type4/sub5) reply, not a 192. Chat/UC still works because UC is NOT assigned by a 189 at all: UserCommConnection::OpenCommunication(@101699) opens the chat channel on nChatServerHandle (set from the LOBBY login's serverHandle in LobbyComm::System::LoggedIn @79368) via transport->vtbl[0x10] — no AssignServer/192 exchange. Hence there is no 'second 189': the prior model wrongly assumed UC and referee were two separate type-4 189s (first→192 UC, second→170 referee). The stub replies 192 to the one-and-only referee 189, so FUN_10021520 never runs, LM+0x580 stays 0, FUN_00462910 no-ops/logs 'Could not initialize RefereeServerConnection.', and RefereeServerConnection::Login retries 5x ([Reconnector] timesClientRetries=5) then aborts → exactly the observed 'connecting to game server' freeze. The login burst's '171 x2' = the client's RegObserverServerList for server_type 4 AND 5 (FUN_00468e80 @83287/83295) — these are what cache the referee server_id→ip:port so step (6) can resolve it.

findings.claim: *(LM+0x580) is a SERVER_ID, written ONLY by FUN_004625d0 (the assigned-referee observer callback), whose param_2 originates from descriptor[0] of an inbound GameServerData(170) on ticket-category 0x108.
findings.evidence: SADK FUN_004625d0 @78286-78299 writes param_2→+0x580, +0x588=60000. tincat3 FUN_10021520 @23744-23756: if(desc[10]==4 && (int)desc+0x29==5){(*(*piVar1+0x20))(&local_8,*param_1,0);} passes *param_1=descriptor[0]=server_id to the observer that reaches FUN_004625d0.

findings.claim: The producer of that 170 is the client's AssignServer(189): FUN_00468f60 calls pGameServerManager(ServerList+0x6c)->vtbl[0x2c](4,4)=tincat3 FUN_10021830, which builds NETMSG 0xBD(189, server_type=4) and registers ticket category 0x108; the matching 170 reply routes (category 0x108) to FUN_10021520.
findings.evidence: SADK FUN_00468f60 @83327 `(*(*(param_1+0x6c)+0x2c))(4,4)`. tincat3 FUN_10021830 @23937-23980: builds 0xbd, sets server_type=param_1, FUN_1002a1c0(...,0x108,AssignServerTicketData), sends via vtbl[0x30]. Receive switch @25847, case 0xaa @26778, category branch `if(iVar7==0x108) FUN_10021520(...)` @26846-26852.

findings.claim: This (4,4) AssignServer is the ONLY type-4 189 the client can emit: it is the sole GameServerManager->vtbl[0x2c] call in SADK.exe with two server-type args, and tincat3's only other 189-builder hardcodes server_type=2.
findings.evidence: grep of SADK for `+0x2c))(<digit>`: line 83327 is the unique `(*(...+0x6c)+0x2c))(4,4)`; all other +0x2c calls are unrelated objects/UI toggles. tincat3 FUN_10027630 @27658-27659 builds 0xbd with server_type=2, category 0x109.

findings.claim: UC/chat is established WITHOUT any AssignServer(189)/UsercommServerData(192): UserCommConnection::OpenCommunication opens the channel on nChatServerHandle (the lobby login serverHandle) via transport->vtbl[0x10]. So replying 192 to the referee 189 is the bug, and there is no separate UC 189.
findings.evidence: SADK UserCommConnection__OpenCommunication @101699-101743 (transport->vtbl[0x10](channelHandle,0)); nChatServerHandle set @79368 inside LobbyComm::System::LoggedIn when connId==main-lobby; opened at GlobalDataLoaded via FUN_00464300(this,nChatServerHandle) @80294. msgdefs 189=AssignServer / 192=UsercommServerData are a request/response pair but UC does not use them.

findings.claim: The [Lobby] url 81.3.59.139:8777 belongs to the NComm Net-Driver master/'site' bootstrap, NOT the TinCat RefereeServerConnection. It is loaded into the same settings object as [Reconnector]timesClientRetries=5 and [Lobby]patchlevel, used by NComm's logon-to-site.
findings.evidence: SADK FUN_0040a390 @11836 hardcodes '81.3.59.139:8777'; the network.ini loader @~28480 reads [Lobby]url (default 81.3.59.139:8777, @28628), [Reconnector]timesClientRetries=5 (@28614), [Lobby]patchlevel (@28639) into one struct; that struct is a member of the NComm net-driver constructed @11990 (NetGUID vftable @11980). 'SendLogonRequest: Connecting to site' is tincat3 FUN_10004660 @3148 — the generic ConnectionManager TCP connect (0xDABAFBEF LOGMEON), address supplied by caller.

findings.claim: FUN_00462910 resolves LM+0x580 as a server_id exactly like CreateVillageServerConnection resolves a list-selected village server_id (same pComm->vtbl[0x38] Resolve + vtbl[0x18] get-handle). So pComm must already have that server_id cached — from the type-4 RegObserverServerList(171/0xab) the client requests at LoadingGlobalData.
findings.evidence: SADK FUN_00462910 @78510 `pComm->vtbl[0x38](*(LM+0x580))`, @78520 `pComm->vtbl[0x18](*(LM+0x580))`. Village twin @79291/79294 with villageServerDesc=GetSelectedVillageServer(server_id from the list). FUN_00468e80 @83287/83295 sends RegObserver for server_type 4 and 5. FUN_10021520's 4/5 branch only sets LM+0x580 and does NOT add to pComm's table (the add path is the else-branch @23758-23760), so the type-4 list 170 is what makes the id resolvable.

findings.claim: The prior model's wireFormat for the 170 reply (server_type=4, server_subtype=5, same ticket_id, plus server_id/ip/port) is correct; its ONLY error was the trigger assumption (expecting a SECOND type-4 189 for the referee while the FIRST goes to UC/192).
findings.evidence: FUN_10021520 gate desc+0x28==4 && desc+0x29==5 confirms the 170 field requirement. The error is visible in the stub: dispatch.py @319 emits the referee 170 only when `conn._uc_assigned` is already True (i.e. on a second type-4 189), and @324-325 routes the first type-4 189 to 192 setting _uc_assigned=True — so the referee 170 is never sent.

traced.answer:
*(LM+0x580) comes from option (a): it is a SERVER_ID handed to the client by the lobby in a GameServerData(170) reply to the client's AssignServer(189), correlated by ticket-category 0x108. Concretely: LobbyManager (state>5) sends ONE AssignServer(189, server_type=4) via GameServerManager::AssignServer (tincat3 FUN_10021830, category 0x108); the lobby must reply with GameServerData(170) carrying the SAME ticket_id and server_type=4 + server_subtype=5; tincat3 FUN_10021520 gates exactly on those two bytes and passes descriptor[0]=server_id to FUN_004625d0, which writes it to LM+0x580. FUN_00462910 then resolves that server_id to ip:port via pComm (vtbl[0x38]/[0x18]) — using the address pComm cached from the type-4 RegObserverServerList — and connects the RefereeServerConnection.

The [Lobby] url 81.3.59.139:8777 is RULED OUT for the TinCat referee. It is the NComm Net-Driver's master/'site' bootstrap endpoint (loaded by FUN_0040a390 / the network.ini loader into the same struct as [Reconnector]timesClientRetries=5 and [Lobby]patchlevel; dialed by tincat3's generic ConnectionManager connect 'SendLogonRequest: Connecting to site', FUN_10004660). It has nothing to do with LM+0x580.

WHAT THE STUB MUST DELIVER (no new info beyond a server_id + its cached address; the referee rides the SAME ip:port the type-4 list advertises):
1. In the type-4 RegObserverServerList(171) response burst, advertise the referee server (GameServerData 170, server_type=4, server_subtype=5, a unique REF server_id, ip=ADVERTISED_IP, port=REFEREE_PORT) so pComm caches REF_id→ip:port. (The stub already does this via _push_to_obs — keep it.)
2. FIX @handler(189): the FIRST (and only) type-4/sub-4 189 MUST be answered with GameServerData(170) echoing the request's ticket_id, server_type=4, server_subtype=5, server_id=REF_id, ip=ADVERTISED_IP, port=REFEREE_PORT — NOT 192. Remove the `conn._uc_assigned` second-189 gate; there is no separate UC 189 (UC opens on the lobby handle). This makes FUN_10021520 fire → LM+0x580=REF_id → FUN_00462910 resolves+binds → Login dials OUR referee.
3. Port: the referee connects to whatever ip:port the REF server_id resolves to in pComm's table — i.e. exactly the ip:port advertised for REF_id in step 1 (ADVERTISED_IP:REFEREE_PORT). Stand up a TinCat listener there that accepts the referee login and pushes LoginSuccess (LobbyMessage category=3, id=0xDCA, one field PermID) so the 5-retry abort is averted.
